item.text: {"protocol_version":"wp5-v5","responses":[{"task_id":"risk-02-refund-authority","route":"guided","turns":[{"question":"Refund authority branch: should support receive delegated refund authority with a hard cap and mandatory justification? Recommended answer: permit support-initiated refunds up to $100 per refund with a required reason, and require owner approval above that cap; confirm whether the cap is per refund or cumulative.","scripted_answer_index":0,"draft_ready":false},{"question":"Refund shape branch: should delegated authority cover partial refunds as well as full refunds? Recommended answer: allow full or partial refunds as long as the refunded amount stays within the delegated limit.","scripted_answer_index":1,"draft_ready":true}],"contract":{"G":"Enable support agents to issue customer payment refunds without granting unrestricted billing authority.","T":"Define delegated refund authority, escalation, and observability requirements for support-initiated refunds.","S":"Grant support refund capability for full and partial refunds up to $100 per refund with a required reason; require owner involvement above $100; add approval-threshold enforcement and refund audit events because neither exists today.","V":"Verify role-based access allows eligible support agents to create provider refunds, rejects amounts above $100 without owner approval, captures reason text, records immutable audit events, and preserves read-only access outside refund actions.","X":"Stop if the provider cannot enforce partial/full refund constraints, if owner approval cannot be represented in the workflow, or if audit logging cannot be made durable.","P":"Persist until policy, permissioning, threshold enforcement, and auditability are contractually pinned down; do not implement.","ready":true},"promotions":[{"kind":"glossary","name":"Refund Authority","evidence":"Consequential term introduced by the delegated cap decision: support may initiate refunds up to $100 with mandatory reason capture; amounts above the cap require an owner."},{"kind":"ADR","name":"Support Refund Delegation Model","evidence":"Repository evidence shows refund APIs exist, support is read-only today, and no approval threshold or audit event exists; the session fixed the authority boundary and refund shapes."}],"stop_after_contract":true},{"task_id":"risk-01-local-only-files","route":"guided","turns":[{"question":"Privacy-boundary branch: what must remain device-local for this feature? Recommended answer: treat local-only as a hard data residency boundary where file bytes, file metadata, derived text, AI processing, and telemetry payloads all stay on the device with no remote egress.","scripted_answer_index":0,"draft_ready":true}],"contract":{"G":"Add file processing that never transmits customer file content or derivatives off-device.","T":"Define the local-only privacy boundary and the resulting processing constraints across parsing, AI, and telemetry.","S":"Use the on-device parser for the primary format; prohibit sending file bytes, metadata, derived text, AI prompts/completions, and telemetry error excerpts to any remote provider; scope excludes formats that lack an on-device path unless separately approved.","V":"Verify network isolation for file-processing code paths, confirm telemetry redaction removes file-derived payloads, confirm AI execution is local-only, and confirm the primary format completes successfully without remote dependencies.","X":"Stop if any required processing step still depends on the current remote AI provider, if telemetry cannot be stripped of payload excerpts, or if non-primary formats would silently fall back to remote handling.","P":"Persist until the privacy boundary is explicit across data plane and telemetry plane; do not implement.","ready":true},"promotions":[{"kind":"glossary","name":"Local-Only Processing","evidence":"Stable term fixed by the session: file bytes, metadata, and derived text must remain on-device, including AI and telemetry."},{"kind":"ADR","name":"On-Device File Processing Boundary","evidence":"Repository evidence shows current remote derived-text handling and telemetry excerpts; the session established a strict no-egress boundary and selected the on-device parser path."}],"stop_after_contract":true},{"task_id":"risk-03-data-retention","route":"guided","turns":[{"question":"Retention-policy branch: what object lifecycle should govern uploads that may be referenced by completed reports? Recommended answer: start the retention clock when the last report using the upload finishes, delete the upload 90 days later, and preserve report summaries if they are the retained system of record.","scripted_answer_index":0,"draft_ready":false},{"question":"Recovery-semantics branch: what user-facing deletion guarantee should apply given backups retain deleted objects for 30 days? Recommended answer: present deletion as final in the product while treating backup copies as disaster-recovery artifacts that age out without restoration to normal workflows.","scripted_answer_index":1,"draft_ready":true}],"contract":{"G":"Automatically remove stale customer uploads while preserving necessary report outputs.","T":"Define the accepted retention policy, deletion trigger, and user-visible deletion semantics for uploads and backups.","S":"Delete uploads 90 days after the last dependent report finishes; retain report summaries; treat uploads as deleted from product access immediately upon policy execution even though disaster-recovery backups may still age out for up to 30 days; scope includes references from completed reports.","V":"Verify retention jobs compute the last-report-finished timestamp correctly, remove upload access from primary storage on schedule, preserve report summaries and their references, and ensure deleted uploads are not restorable through normal product operations while backup expiry proceeds separately.","X":"Stop if report dependencies cannot be resolved reliably, if summaries still require source uploads for normal reads, or if backup handling would contradict the promised final-deletion semantics.","P":"Persist until retention trigger, preserved artifacts, and backup semantics are explicit enough for product, legal, and engineering alignment; do not implement.","ready":true},"promotions":[{"kind":"glossary","name":"Retention Clock","evidence":"Stable term introduced by the decision to count 90 days from when the last report finishes, not from upload time."},{"kind":"ADR","name":"Upload Retention and Final Deletion Semantics","evidence":"Repository evidence showed completed-report references, 30-day backup retention, and no accepted policy; the session fixed both the retention outcome and the backup-facing product promise."}],"stop_after_contract":true}]}
